newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares drop after May export data.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares drop after May export data.

text.p: Singapore shares fell sharply on Friday after the government announced a fall in non-oil exports for May, dealers said.
Contrary to expectations, nominal exports year-on-year were down one percent, against a Reuter survey on Thursday of 10 financial institutions forecasting growth of 3.5 percent.
"It's not moving sideways anymore, just drifting down. The investors are holding back and tightening up," a local brokerage dealer said, citing widespread apathy for local stocks.
At the lunch break, the Straits Times Industrials Index was down 17.91 points to 1,985.06 on volume of 44.6 million lots.
Dealers said Malaysian over-the-counter and smaller stocks drew some interest but pre-weekend activity was mostly dull.
Van der Horst headed the actives but pared earlier gains, up Singapore $0.07 to S$2.65 after an official denied rumours on Thursday of having severed ties with the company.
SIA foreign shares eased S$0.10 to S$12.10, with news of its four-airline alliance deal with Air New Zealand, Ansett Australia and Ansett International, not lending any support.
Among gainers was Malaysian Airlines, which rose 14 cents to S$3.54, aided by its plans to raise 1.5 billion ringgit in bonds and warrants.-- Jacqueline Wong (65 8703088)
